summary: How postwar defense money, isolated suburbs and anti-communist activism made Orange County, California a hothouse of the hard right, embodied by John Birch Society congressman and 1972 American Party presidential candidate John Schmitz.

evidence.note: Cold War defense spending identified as the engine of Orange County's growth
1920s Klan strength in Anaheim and Fullerton; county conservative from the start
The Fundamentals essays (1910-1915) funded by county oil man Lyman Stewart; earliest covered period
1960 uproar over a school board member hosting an ACLU meeting starts the organized movement
1961 anti-communism school in Anaheim draws thousands, Birchers call Eisenhower a communist tool
Fred Schwarz and his Christian Anti-Communist Crusade get an extended segment
Schmitz elected to the state senate as its first John Birch Society member
Schmitz writes introduction to a Jewish-elite conspiracy book in 1971
1972 American Party presidential run after Wallace is shot
1982 exposure of his second family ends his political career
closing segment on his daughter Mary Kay Letourneau and her abuse of a pupil

notes: Two primaries: part 1 is Orange County as a place, part 2 John Schmitz. Roles apply to Schmitz only. Covered span starts at the 1910-1915 Fundamentals segment (county prehistory around 1900 is vaguer) and ends with Schmitz's 2001 death; Trump comparisons are commentary, so reaches_present is false. Letourneau segment is short and not detailed, so no child-abuse theme or warning; the 1973 drowning of Schmitz's son gets child-death.
